decisive_items: Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side
Negative P waves in lead I
QRS complexes in leads V1 through V6 showing activation of ventricle in right thorax
response.rationale: Echocardiogram and ECG clearly demonstrate dextrocardia with situs inversus, which explains the reversed cardiac anatomy and ECG findings. The coronary occlusion and troponin elevation are secondary complications, not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Describes acute MI, which is a consequence of the underlying dextrocardia with situs inversus, not the most likely primary diagnosis.
Hepatic dullness on the left is due to situs inversus, not cor pulmonale; no evidence of right heart failure from pulmonary disease.
